definitions.explanation: Reading text quickly by scanning rather than reading every word carefully. The literal image is of reading 'diagonally' across the page rather than line by line.

examples.japanese: {新聞|しんぶん}を{斜|なな}め{読|よ}みする。
{時間|じかん}がないので{斜|なな}め{読|よ}みで{済|す}ませた。
examples.english: I didn't have time, so I just skimmed through it.

examples.japanese: {斜|なな}め{読|よ}みでは{大事|だいじ}なポイントを{見落|みお}としてしまうことがある。
examples.english: When skimming, you may overlook important points.

notes:
Literally 'diagonal reading' ({斜|なな}め 'diagonal, slanted' + {読|よ}み 'reading'). The image is of eyes moving diagonally across the page rather than following each line. Used as a noun or with する as a verb ({斜|なな}め{読|よ}みする). A useful and commonly encountered word in everyday Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {斜|なな}め{読|よ}みする: to skim-read
- {斜|なな}め{読|よ}みで{済|す}ませる: to get by with just skimming
- {新聞|しんぶん}の{斜|なな}め{読|よ}み: skimming through the newspaper

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {読|よ}み{流|なが}す: to skim over — a verb meaning to read without paying close attention
- {速読|そくどく}: speed reading — a more formal term, often used for trained speed-reading techniques
- {拾|ひろ}い{読|よ}み: selective reading — picking out only certain parts to read
